Keeping peptides cool in Palm Springs

Palm Springs Regional Airport, about 2.5 miles northeast of the city's center point, is the nearest NOAA normals station.28 Its July and August average highs are 108.6 °F and 108.1 °F, and July nights average 79.4 °F.8 Highs average above 100 °F from June (103.6 °F) through September (101.8 °F), and the airport averages 115 days a year at 100 °F or more.87 Winter is gentle by comparison. December averages 69.2 °F by day and 46.2 °F at night, and a freezing night comes about 0.3 times a year.87

Stability differs from one peptide to the next: GenScript notes that each peptide's stability is unique and depends on its sequence.10 Bachem, a peptide maker, says its products are typically shipped at ambient temperature, with the recommended long-term storage condition noted on the label.9 For comparison, one FDA-approved freeze-dried peptide, EGRIFTA SV (tesamorelin), is labeled for storage at 20 to 25 °C, with excursions permitted from 15 to 30 °C (59 to 86 °F).11 That is one product's tested limit, not a rule for other peptides. The airport's average July high, 108.6 °F, works out to about 42.6 °C, well past that range.8 The storage guide explains where each kind of vial belongs once it is indoors.

About Palm Springs

Palm Springs had an estimated 45,315 residents on July 1, 2025.1 That is up about 1.7% from its 2020 base of 44,575 but 100 fewer than a year earlier, and it ranks 18th among the county's 28 incorporated cities.1 Its 94.5 square miles of land exceed the 81.1 square miles of Riverside, the county seat, which has about seven times as many people.21 The city sits about 107 miles east of Los Angeles, at 487 feet above sea level.12 The Cahuilla name for the area, Sec-he ("boiling water"), refers to the hot springs at what is now the center of the business district.13 The Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians is the city's largest landowner: of its roughly 32,000-acre reservation, about 6,700 acres lie inside city limits.13

The City Council set up a process for recognizing neighborhood organizations in 2005, and 52 are recognized as of October 2026.14 They include Deepwell Estates, Historic Tennis Club, The Movie Colony, Old Las Palmas, Twin Palms and Warm Sands.14 Palm Canyon Drive is where the city stages its parades and festivals, and its Walk of Stars carries the names of many Hollywood legends.12 The Palm Springs Aerial Tramway carries riders to about 8,500 feet on Mount San Jacinto in about 15 minutes.12 At the top is the high country of a 14,000-acre state park and wilderness with more than 50 miles of trails, crowned by San Jacinto Peak (10,834 feet), the highest peak in the California State Park System.15 Palm Springs International Airport served more than 3.3 million passengers in 2025, a record and about 2.4% more than in 2024.16

The city's hospital has deep roots. Desert Regional Medical Center began as Desert Hospital, built by the Desert Healthcare District on the grounds of the former El Mirador Hotel.17 The hotel had earlier been converted into the 1,600-bed Torney General Hospital for wounded soldiers.17 Tenet now runs Desert Regional as a 385-bed acute-care hospital.17 In March 2023 the Riverside County Emergency Medical Services Agency made it the Coachella Valley's first Level 1 trauma center; it logged 4,807 trauma arrivals in 2022.18 It also trains doctors. A five-year general surgery residency was due to start that July with six residents, growing to 15.18 From 2015 until July 1, 2020, it housed the UC Riverside School of Medicine's family medicine residency, 24 residents in all, before the program moved to San Bernardino.19

The median age is 58.5 years.20 Only 7.9% of residents are under 18, and 35.3% are 65 or older.20 More than a quarter of workers (26.0%) work from home.21 About 27% of housing units, 9,975 of 36,813, are held for seasonal, recreational or occasional use.2223

Nearby

Straight-line distances from the city's center put Cathedral City about 5 miles east-northeast and Rancho Mirage about 7 miles east-southeast.2 Desert Hot Springs is about 11 miles north, Palm Desert about 11 miles east-southeast and La Quinta about 19 miles southeast.2 The county hub, Peptides in Riverside, covers Riverside, about 50 miles west, and the locations page lists the rest.2

Frequently asked questions

Is semaglutide a GLP-1 inhibitor?

No. In PubChem, the chemistry database of the National Library of Medicine, the FDA pharmacology summary classes semaglutide as a GLP-1 receptor agonist: it activates the GLP-1 receptor rather than blocking it. The same record describes it as a polypeptide of 31 amino acids.4 Its CAS registry number is 910463-68-2.5 For the published research and its regulatory status, read What is Semaglutide?.

Which ZIP codes cover Palm Springs?

Two main ones. In the Census Bureau's 2020 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, 92264 covers about 48.1% of the city's land and 92262 about 34.6%, and the rest falls in other ZIP areas.6 Every one of them is served the same way, with orders shipping from the USA and Canada like all orders across the United States. The shipping page explains how to choose a ship-from origin and what to check when a parcel arrives.

How hot has it been in Palm Springs?

Recent summers have set records. In NOAA's daily records for Palm Springs Regional Airport, which begin in February 1998, the hottest day was July 5, 2024, at 124 °F, followed by 123 °F on June 17, 2021.3 In July 2024, 29 of 31 days reached 110 °F or more.3 That year logged 135 days at 100 °F or more, against a 1991 to 2020 normal of 115.37 Bring a delivered parcel indoors promptly.
